outcome.summary: After the corrected importer deployed, 28 sequential authenticated manual cabinet shard deliveries refreshed every CIA World Leaders page (197 countries applied; Bosnia and Herzegovina skipped closed on the page schema, as in both rehearsals). With a fresh read-only recovery point taken and every Vercel cron job paused, the approved one-time repair applied the production plan in one transaction (5,715 row changes, 5,715 history rows). Every postflight check passed, a new plan proposed nothing, and production's cabinet-table totals equal the second rehearsal's final totals.

observations: The production plan's categories, observations, target counts, and expected history rows are identical to the second rehearsal's repair plan.
Each nine-country delivery completed in 81 to 82 seconds (shard 26, with three countries, in 20 seconds); the README had budgeted about 227 seconds per shard from an earlier measurement.
The README's production sequence named 27 deliveries with shard 27 empty; the controller also delivered shard 27, which returned the empty-shard response and crawled nothing.

The scheduled pulse.v2.ingest run at 08:00 UTC ended failed (HTTP 502, partial) during the refresh. It touches no cabinet data and is unrelated to DAT-037; the data-reliability monitor has recorded partial Pulse ingests from an upstream timeout on earlier days. Not investigated here.
Legacy hand-entered dates remain on 8 roster-typed terms (P1 disclosure): five United States rows stay current and three United Kingdom rows are retired, exactly as in the second rehearsal.
7 retired CIA-owned terms carry no provenance (P3 disclosure), as in the second rehearsal.
limitations: The recovery point and plan files stay outside the repository; their hashes are recorded here, and the controller deletes the recovery point after closure.
CIA pages were read on 2026-09-29; later page updates flow through the daily shard, not this record.
Freshness for shard 2 was not stamped because Bosnia and Herzegovina failed closed; the source timestamp was stamped by later shards.
The pause covered every Vercel cron job for 3 minutes 48 seconds; one scheduled Pulse clustering slot was skipped and is not backfilled.
The public policy page does not yet state the APR-D173 prelaunch waiver.
The Codex monitor's two cabinet incidents live in its gitignored local output in the main checkout, not in the repository; this record is their closure evidence.
